newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao gets bail but must surrender passport.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao gets bail but must surrender passport.

text.p: An Indian court on Tuesday ordered former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to surrender his passport after granting him bail in a case involving an alleged conspiracy to smear a political foe.
The Delhi High Court accepted Rao's bail application in the forgery case. The Congress party leader was made to pay a bail bond of 100,000 rupees ($2,800) and surety of the same amount.
Rao and three other accused -- former cabinet minister K.K. Tewary, Hindu guru Chandraswami and his private secretary -- had previously been granted temporary bail in the case.
"There appears to be no apprehension at this stage of their fleeing from justice or tampering with evidence," United News of India quoted Judge S.K. Mahajan as saying.
But after granting them indefinite bail, which protects them from arrest during trial, the court ordered the four to surrender their passports to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
The federal agency charged Rao and the others with using forged documents in 1989 in a bid to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, who later became prime minister.
The CBI has accused them of forging bank documents to show that Singh's son, Ajeya Singh, had a secret bank account with large amounts of money on the Caribbean island of St Kitts.

While Rao won a breather on Tuesday, he is battling to save his political future in two other criminal cases. On Wednesday, a court is due to hear his request for indefinite bail in a three-year-old bribery case.
Legislators of a regional party say they were paid $100,000 to vote against a 1993 no-confidence motion which Rao's Congress-led government survived by a wafer-thin margin.
Earlier this year, the CBI accused Rao and other Congress leaders of buying the votes. They have denied any wrongdoing.
Rao has won temporary protection against arrest in this case, in which the CBI has yet to file charges.
In a third case, an Indian expatriate businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, alleges that Rao and Chandraswami conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983. Rao has said he is innocent.
